summary: The lecture covers Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Indian Constitution — Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP). It explains their origin (Ireland), non-justiciable nature, distinction from Fundamental Rights, classification (Socialist, Gandhian, Liberal-Intellectual), key articles (38-51), and the 86th Amendment (2002) inserting Article 21A and modifying Article 45.
points: Part IV (Articles 36–51) contains Directive Principles of State Policy, a novel feature per Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
Borrowed from the Irish Constitution; aim to guide governance for social welfare and human rights.
Non-justiciable (Article 37): courts cannot enforce; government may implement at its discretion.
Fundamental Rights (USA) are justiciable, political democracy; DPSP (Ireland) are non-justiciable, socio-economic democracy.
Scholars classify DPSP into Socialist, Gandhian, and Liberal-Intellectual principles.
Art 38: Minimise income inequalities; Art 39: Equal pay for equal work, protect children's health.
Art 39A: Free legal aid; Art 40: Village panchayats; Art 41: Aid to elderly, sick, disabled.
Art 42: Maternity relief; Art 43: Living wage, promote cottage/cooperative industries.
Art 43A: Workers' participation in management; Art 43B: Promote cooperative societies.
Art 44: Uniform Civil Code; Art 45: Early childhood care/education for under-6 children.
Art 46: Promote SC/ST educational/economic interests; Art 47: Prohibition of intoxicating drinks.
Art 48: Organise agriculture/animal husbandry; Art 49: Protect national monuments.
Art 50: Separate judiciary from executive; Art 51: Promote international peace and security.
86th Amendment Act, 2002: Inserted Art 21A (free compulsory education 6–14 years as Fundamental Right) and revised Art 45 to cover 0–6 years.

check.q: From which country's constitution were the Directive Principles of State Policy borrowed?
Which article declares that DPSP are non-justiciable and not enforceable by courts?
What change did the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 make to Article 45?
opts: Shifted its focus to early childhood care for 0–6 years
